title: Longlée to Henri IV, duplicate of a dispatch from Madrid [Dec 1589 - Feb 1590]: unpublished, read in part (63.7% certain words; 88.7% with probable)

documents.route: Pierre de Ségusson, sieur de Longlée, Madrid -> Henri IV

plaintext.source: No decipherment known; not in Mousset 1912 (nothing between 15 Oct 1588 and 3 Mar 1590).

transcription.notes: Shapes labelled with a frozen atlas; doubtful signs re-read blind by Brice Dudout on five plates (2 and 11 Nov 2026; rules pre-registered, controls passed); see BLIND-REREADING.md.

system.summary: Longlée’s nomenclator: an alphabet of homophonic signs (letters, digits, symbols) and a few signs for short words; the same hand as the two edited letters of the volume. Starting point: the table printed by Mousset (pp. lviii–lix), corrected on the hand of these copies

prior_solution.where: Mousset 1912 (two sister letters only); Cryptiana (henryiii) mentions the three BNE letters without a reading; this repository (no entry); quick search of Ruble and CSP Foreign 1589-96.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

By hand this is mostly an artefact: the script gives no letter for the 137 {A|B} hesitation tokens (first label S1 = s) and aligned only 64% because the transcription has f. 67v first. A decoder from key_K4.tsv, first label used, reproduces decryption.txt except at labels the key file lacks (N_ROI 'le roi', N_PORTUGAL 'portugal', DOT x30 and four marks without a value, ZG printed '?'); those with a shown value are now in key_K4_supplement.tsv, listed in outcome.key_file; key_K4.tsv unchanged. decryption.txt against reading.md in page order: 8 of 335 words outside brackets hold a letter the decrypt does not give; 12 places in words given as certain differ without a mark (part du duc for 'partdeduc', l'argent for 'laigent', qu'il for 'quel', d'auantaige for 'dauentaige', Mate for 'mat', letters left out in Roisieu, s'attend, chacun, demandes, accorder). Reading not changed.

Second round of the decrypt audit: the 12 places where a word given as certain differs from decryption.txt were not marked in reading.md, because the file's only mark, {x}, is a class of the contributor's count; they stay listed in NOTES. One legend line added to reading.md (contributor's reading, not the output of the key; decryption.txt is) and one note line to the header of decryption.txt (labels missing from the repository key_K4.tsv; y printed i). Then the places of the 16 Nov 2026 decrypt audit still unmarked were marked {x}: du, qu'il, quant, s'attend, d'auantaige, Mate (f. 67r), chacun, demandes. validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): key K4 frozen, then one measurement on the reserved part of the 1 April 1590 letter (f. 65r + f. 65v ll. 1-13, 1561 letters, never looked at before) against Mousset 1912 pp. 394-396: characters 0.874 vs 200 shuffled-key controls max 0.361 (mean 0.304); words 0.647 (controls max 0.154). texts.label: Longlée to Henri IV, duplicate of a dispatch, Madrid [Dec 1589 - Feb 1590] (BNE Mss/994 ff. 67r-67v)
texts.summary: Pierre de Ségusson, sieur de Longlée, the French resident at Madrid, wrote in cipher to Henry IV early in 1590. The packet was intercepted: its copy, “Dupp. d’une despesche”, is now in the Biblioteca Nacional de España, with two other letters of Longlée that the Spaniards had deciphered by Luis Valle de la Cerda. Those two letters (3 March and 1 April 1590) were edited by Albert Mousset in 1912 from the originals at the French Foreign Office; this one was not, and no contemporary decipherment accompanies the copy. We publish the reading as far as we could take it, gaps included: 88.7% of the words certain or probable, 63.7% certain (20 Nov 2026), below the 95% threshold we hold ourselves to. It shows an envoy of the Duke of Mercœur at Madrid asking that Philip II declare openly against Henry IV and seize the goods of royalist Frenchmen.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #820 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the contributor-side entry of 11 Nov 2026 (grade B, Claude Opus 5.5 for Brice Dudout). reading.md was read as French sentences against translation.md and recounted from its marks: 479 cipher words, 305 certain, 120 probable, 9 restored, 45 unresolved (estimated words per segment), so 305/479 = 0.637 sure (f. 67r 203/311, f. 67v 102/168). A decoder written by the reviewer from key_K4.tsv and key_K4_supplement.tsv reproduces decryption.txt on all 46 lines. F. 67r builds sentences throughout: the duplicate sent by Bayonne, no preparations beyond the fleet of sixty or eighty ships against the English, the arrival on the 21st of Tornasoni for the Duke of Mercoeur, what he is thought to ask of Philip II, Roisieux expected for Mayenne, money given to keep the war going. Its last sentence (the duke 'de Portugal', the government of the Low Countries, Savoy asking for help) is in pieces. F. 67v is coherent in clauses with a hole in most of them: Sessa to Rome, Olivares to withdraw, no dispatch since 3 November, 'la defence de l'eglise catholique'. Coherent but raw; read in part. The English is a summary, not a translation. An untested suggestion of this review, not part of the reading and not counted: lines 29 to 30 of f. 67r (decrypt 'sleducdeportugalmeconltinlera ... augoulernee / mentdespaibbas') may read 'le duc de Parme continuera encor quelque temps au gouuernement des pais bas'; it needs three sign shapes looked at on the image (f67r-29, positions 9, 19 and 41, counted from 0). Not checked against the DECODE images. A model's reading: no person has checked it.
